windows.cross-object-flush: one flush of a keyed amendment of each of many distinct objects its transaction already read and buffered — the pre-commit flush, or a requesting case's read-dependency flush a later read causes — over a provider-free port offering ordered transport, read as two regions: planning, from finalization's start to the finalized plan, whose retained bytes are a separate checkpoint before any Write Group executes; and execution, summed over every Write Group's steps through lowering, production bind adaptation, psycopg's serialization, and presentation, with each group's completion between regions and inside neither; a flush reaching deferred spans adds a third region, summed over every advance of a span's range binding through span preparation, the coverage reads the port answers, and binding of the ready group the next execution region runs, and counts its coverage reads; the reads before the flush, the authored inputs, admission, and the commit precede or follow every region; per-object bytes divide a flush's by its objects
windows.keyed-write: one public Typed or Wire keyed verb over a row its transaction already read, or one target write over a row its transaction never read, until transact returns: preparation, buffering, the pre-commit flush's settlement and SQL lowering, production bind adaptation, psycopg's document serialization, and the commit; a target's own coverage read at flush over provider-free rows, but no earlier read and no database execution
windows.model-preparation: one complete model preparation from the declared Entity Classes
windows.wire-insert-response: one public tx.wire.insert of a nested, polymorphic Create Payload inside an open transaction, from the payload arriving to the frozen node it answers; no flush, lowering, or serialization
